title: Differentiable Timing-Driven FPGA Placement with Smooth Optimization and ML-Based Delay Calibration
problem: FPGA placement must simultaneously minimize wirelength and optimize timing metrics (TNS/WNS), but traditional placement algorithms struggle with multi-objective optimization and accurate timing estimation.
motivation: Placement is critical for timing closure in FPGA design; faster convergence enables more efficient design iterations.
method: Differentiable optimization framework with timing preconditioning to smooth the objective landscape, multiplier scheduling scheme for multi-objective balancing, and XGBoost-based machine learning model for net delay prediction to improve timing estimation accuracy.
key_novelty: Combining smooth differentiable optimization with ML-based delay calibration for timing-driven FPGA placement.
contributions: Novel timing preconditioning method that smooths the timing objective landscape
General multiplier scheduling scheme for multi-objective optimization
XGBoost-based net delay prediction model for improved timing estimation
limitations: Evaluated only on ISPD 2016 contest benchmarks; generalization to other benchmark suites unclear.
